title: The Cistern That Would Not Stop Filling
story: Deep in the Tideshell Cistern, Grottomaw the Cistern Eel coils around a stone siphon and pumps seawater into the chamber, giggling in bubbles. Three pearl-divers are stranded on a ledge 24 feet above the water, and the eel's siphon pours in 8 feet of water every minute. Mr 6 dives down, wedges his sword into the old drain grate, and the drain begins sucking water back out at 5 feet per minute.
question: With the siphon pouring in 8 feet per minute and the drain pulling out 5 feet per minute, how many minutes do the divers have before the water reaches their ledge 24 feet up?
solution: Each minute the water really rises by 8 - 5 = 3 feet.
The ledge is 24 feet above the water, so 24 / 3 = 8.
The divers have 8 minutes to climb to safety.
praise: Working with the rates was exactly right — the missing step was subtracting the drain from the siphon to find how fast the water TRULY rises.
hint: Water comes in and water goes out at the same time. What is the water's net gain in one single minute?
victory: The divers scrambled up the rope with a full minute to spare, and Grottomaw kept pumping so hard that he flushed himself right out the drain into the open sea. Mr 6 waved goodbye with his cape dripping and his math dry.
imagePrompt: A giant pale eel coiled around a stone siphon in a green-lit flooding sea cave, water swirling toward a drain grate while a brave numeral-6 knight in a blue cape braces his sword against it and three divers cling to a high ledge.
